To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activity of Pd/TiO2 and Pt/TiO2 was higher than Pp/ZrO2 and Pd/ZrO2 for hydrogen combustion reaction.
Pd and Pt ions substituted ZrO2 and TiO2 were active for the catalytic hydrogen combustion and the reaction was proposed to proceed through a different mechanism over ZrO2 as compared to TiO2.
the catalytic hydrogen combustion over the ionic supported catalysts is a surface reaction and the reaction over Zr(OH)(4) supported catalysts is different from the reaction over Ti(OH)(4).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of noble metal catalysts in ionic form and the study of the catalytic hydrogen combustion mechanism.
the development of a novel catalyst system for catalytic hydrogen oxidation reaction and the mechanism of the reaction is proposed by using the spectroscopic observations.
the synthesis and catalytic hydrogen combustion studies over Pd and Pt ions substituted TiO(,2) and ZrO(,2).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction over the ZrO( 2) supported catalyst was proposed to be a redox mechanism while that over the TiO( 2 ) supported catalyst was proposed as a hybrid mechanism.
the activity of the ionic noble metal catalysts is dependent upon the support and its interaction with the metal ion.
the reaction over the ZrO( 2) supported catalyst was a redox mechanism while over the TiO(2)-supported catalysts, it was a redox and Mars van Krevelen mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activity of the catalysts for the reaction was dependent on the support and not on the metal.
the catalytic hydrogen combustion over the noble metal ion substituted supports can be explained by two different mechanisms.
the reaction over the ZrO( 2)-supported catalysts is more selective for hydrogen oxidation while the reaction over the TiO(2)-supported catalyst is more selective for CO oxidation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalytic activity is not only governed by the support but is also dependent on the metal ions.
the catalytic activity of noble metals in the combustion of hydrogen depends not only on the nature of the noble metal but also on the support.
the activity of noble metals can be improved by substituting the support in ionic form.
